name: W Sardinia, Poltu Quatu
positioning: A Mediterranean resort in Poltu Quatu, a village hidden in a granite-cliff fjord, at the edge of a marina that is the jumping-off point for the La Maddalena Archipelago, with Sardinian-heritage design and a social pool deck
best_for: Couples and friends who want a stylish Sardinian base for boat days to La Maddalena
Travelers who like design and culture, from local art to nuragic sites

facts.text: Poltu Quatu means 'hidden port' in the local Sardinian dialect.
The hotel is at the edge of a marina, minutes away from beaches.
Rooms have whitewashed walls and cedar joinery.
Deluxe and Studio Suites have private terraces.
TANIT serves local seafood with views over the marina.
Experiences include local vineyard visits and a tasting led by a local shepherd.
Guests can explore the nuragic landscape of Arzachena, with ancient stone towers and monumental tombs.
Through Liquid Art System, internationally recognized artworks turn the hotel into a diffused gallery.

highlights.text: The village sits in a natural fjord of granite cliffs and is hidden from view from the sea until you sail inside.
Poltu Quatu Marina, a few steps from the hotel, is a departure point for the La Maddalena Archipelago national park, a short boat ride away.
The design uses organic forms, local materials and handcrafted touches inspired by ancient art and traditional pottery.
The WET Deck pool is relaxed by day and turns to music, events and a social atmosphere at sunset.

considerations.text: A rental car is needed to explore the island further.
The hotel is at the edge of a marina, minutes from the beaches rather than on one.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires travel planning to reach main attractions.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: W Sardinia, Poltu Quatu
